{{MultipleIssues|citation|expand}}
{{Quote|Kajidics?''"<br />"''Criminal syndicates.|[[Malik Carr]] and [[Nom Anor]] on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]]|<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref>}}
'''Kajidic''' was the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] philosophy which guided most of daily life and politics in Hutt families. It was developed by the Hutt [[Budhila Hestilic Amura]] after the Hutts relocated to [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]], following the [[Hutt Cataclysms]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] word ''kajidic'' is said to literally mean "Somebody's got to have it. Why not us?"<ref name="SWR12">[[Star Wars (1998) 12|''Star Wars'' (1998) 12]]</ref>

[[File:BesadiiBanner-HuntForZiro.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The banner of the [[Besadii/Legends|Besadii]] kajidic]]
''Kajidic'' was also a loose Hutt term for their clans, their "business enterprises" and criminal syndicates, and for the archetypal superclan they believed was destined to eventually rule [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Separate clans would usually run their own kajidic in competition with other clans'. The kajidics were governed by the [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Hutt Grand Council]], which oversaw their operations, and each kajidic had an appointed leader, called a [[Kajidii/Legends|kajidii]] or lorda.

The [[Vodran (species)/Legends|Vodrans]], as vassals of the Hutts, also organized themselves in [[Miniature kajidic|kajidics]], though these were wholly subservient to Hutt kajidics.

==Philosophy==
The initial philosophy of kajidic, as expressed by Budhila, was that of fierce competition, which always allowed the strong to survive over the weak. It was also influenced soon after their contact with [[human/Legends|humans]]; it taught that galactic civilization would not be conquered by territorial or military subjugation, but would be controled and exploited by infiltration and influence.<ref name="TEA" />

The philogophy became so ingrained in the Hutt society and their [[clan]] operations while dealing with each other and with other species, that the term came to be synonymous with "clan".<ref name="TEA" />

==Hutt Kajidics==
The Hutt Kajidics were criminal/business syndicates run as families by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] and had their hands in all kinds of criminal ventures. Unlike the usual crime syndicate that operated in secret, the Hutt clans operated in the open, claiming leadership over dozens of worlds. The Kajidics employed those of all species as vassals, such as the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] and [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]].<ref name="SAV">[[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']]</ref>

Though once in constant conflict with each other&mdash;such as during the [[Hutt Cataclysms]]&mdash;the Hutt clans were kept in order by the [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Hutt Grand Council]], the ruling body of the entire Hutt species, [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], and Hutt clans. However, some rivalries could not be contained, as was the case with the prominent [[Besadii/Legends|Besadiis]] and [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijics]], who were bitter enemies,<ref name="Magazine 21">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine 21|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine'' 21]]</ref> and the [[Nem'ro clan|Nem'ro]] and [[Fa'athra clan|Fa'athra]] clans, both of whom had members that were major rivals.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

Several Kajidics had produced some very successful Hutts, such as [[Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo/Legends|Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo]],<ref name="Magazine 21" /> [[Jiliac Desilijic Tiron]], and [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], all from clan Desilijic that proved to be very successful [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]]. Clan [[Besadii/Legends|Besadii]] also produced some successful crime lords, such as [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla the Elder]], [[Aruk Besadii Aora]] and [[Durga Besadii Tai]], as did clan [[Anjiliac]], such as [[Mika Anjiliac Chiera]], a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] crime lord,<ref name="TF">''[[Tempest Feud]]''</ref> and [[Kajidii/Legends|Kajidii]] [[Vedo Anjiliac Atirue]].<ref name="THG">''[[The Hutt Gambit]]''</ref> The [[Illip]] clan produced the famous scientist [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Juvard Illip Oggurobb]].<ref name="Rise">{{TORweb|url=rothc|text=Rise of the Hutt Cartel}}</ref>

==Hutt crime lords==
{{Quote|I am a kajidic lorda. I have a duty to my people to show that nobody gets away with an outrage like this. If we let such outrages go unpunished, what would happen to our civilization?|Jabba Desilijic Tiure|<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' novelization]]</ref>}}
The Hutts were notorious for their ruthlessness and success in the underworld. Many Hutts would ransack ships for their cargo. As masters of the criminal underworld, they would steal, cheat, and murder without regret. They often hired [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] such as [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] to transport illegal [[Spice/Legends|spice]]. They would often have a fortress of some kind, often on remote planets, such as [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] on Tatooine. Hutt fortresses would usually be guarded by selected [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] or [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. Gamorreans and [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] were common [[Species/Legends|species]] to fulfill this duty. Leading an organization of crooks and scum meant competition. The Hutts that got involved with criminal activity were often killed, or [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]]. Only the more cunning and clever Hutts, like Jabba, stayed at the top of the food chain. Some Hutts, like Jabba, had such an influence that they controlled entire planets. However, a few Hutts didn't follow the lifestyle of a crime lord and stick to their Kajidics' criminal activities, such as [[Juvard Illip Oggurobb|Juvard]] of the [[Illip]] clan, who became a droid engineer.<ref name="Rise" />

Hutt kingpins often had torture chambers to deal with failures and unwanted guests. Other Hutts had pets which they would watch in enjoyment as the victim was devoured. Gardulla the Hutt had a [[Gardulla's krayt dragon|krayt dragon]], which, in irony, opened its jaws to receive her after [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] interrogated her about a [[Bando Gora/Legends|mysterious cult]]. Jabba the Hutt had [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|his own rancor]], which would eat anyone who fell into the pit beneath his audience chamber.
